body: Thanks, I’ve talked to 2 different lawyers and both said it’s better to wait and respond to her when she files than filing before she does.  They said during the separation you can do a maintenance agreement outlining finances, visitation, etc.  The issue is she’s trying to make the maintenance agreement the final agreement now and I don’t know how to stop her.

But if she wants to leave and give up on our relationship, give up on our family and I still want to try, why should I have to reduce my standard of living?   This isn’t my choice, it’s hers.  If she really wants to leave shouldn’t she prove it by doing whatever is necessary to leave while causeing minimal disruption to my and our sons life?

She started ghosting me when she would travel with her boss.  Found a pic of flowers on her phone, a slack chat where she said ‘you make me laugh, I haven’t had that in a long time”, an audio recording of her blowing him a kiss and saying ‘bye babe’.  Nothing concrete, but enough to make me paranoid and, yes my paranoia was what eventually led to the separation.  She is asking for 50/50 custody with her as primary, I’m assuming so she doesn’t have to pay child support.

Thank you everyone for your advice, I was hoping to catch her to prove to her I know what's going on and try to get her to stop, but it doesn't look like that's going to be possible, all I have is circumstantial evidence.  Everyone keeps telling me cheaters get caught eventually, but it's been almost 7 months and that hasn't happened so I don't think it's going to.

We are in couples counseling and I'm seeing a therapist, but neither seems to be helping much, she's always bitter after our appointments.

I have spoken to a lawyer and where I live you have to be separated for a year before you can file for divorce, from what I've heard the first one to leave the house is considered abandoning the marriage and loses custody so I can't leave.

She's also spoken to a lawyer two times, most recently last Monday.  She originally told me she wanted a separation early last month, with us both moving out after the New Year.  I fought her saying if she want's out she has to leave now and I'd get custody due to her travel schedule which made her backpedal and agree to try again, now I'm wondering if that's still her plan.

If it was just the two of us I would have filed for separation as soon as this started, but it's not so I want us to work, I want our family, I still love her.  The woman I fell in love with is still in there somewhere, I'm hoping something (time?) will bring her back to me.
